items.question: Why is my Google Places API key rejected?
steps: Open the Google Cloud project that owns the key and confirm Places API (New) is enabled.
Check that the project has an active billing account and the key permits Places API (New).

Heimdall sends requests from its backend. Browser HTTP-referrer restrictions do not fit this request path. For IP restrictions, ask support for the deployed backend outbound IPs; do not disable restrictions as a workaround.
Copy the key without spaces, reconnect it in Scrape → Google Places, and try again. A connected key is not proof that a provider search will succeed.

items.question: How do I fix a Google quota or billing error?
steps: Open Google Cloud billing for the project and check its payment status. Premium does not pay Google API fees.
Review Places API quotas and current usage in the same project. If you reached a quota, wait for its reset or decide whether to change it in Google Cloud.
Review provider pricing before raising a quota or retrying. One Heimdall Google search can make multiple billable requests.

items.question: Why are there no results, or fewer than my target?
steps: Try a clear query such as restaurants in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. Check the spelling and include the country if the city name is ambiguous.
Try a broader business category or nearby location. A target is a maximum, not a guaranteed result count.
Google Places keeps operational businesses without a website listed in the returned record, so many checked candidates may not qualify.
Review the completion message before retrying. Repeating searches may incur additional provider charges.

items.question: What should I do if a search fails or times out?
steps: Read the error shown in Heimdall and check your internet connection. If your session expired, sign in and reconnect your provider key.
Check your provider console for errors or service restrictions. Wait before retrying a temporary failure; avoid repeatedly starting the same search.
If it continues, email support@heimdall.life with the method, time, and error text. Never send your API key, password, or verification code.

items.question: Why is my Foursquare key rejected?
steps: Open your Foursquare Places project and use its Service API key, not a client ID, client secret, or an old credential for another API.
Check that your project has access to the supported Places API and that its plan and billing permit the request. A rejection can mean a key or access problem, not just a typing error.
Paste only the key, without a Bearer prefix or surrounding spaces, into Scrape → Foursquare Business Discovery and reconnect.

items.question: How do I fix a Foursquare request-limit or billing error?
steps: Check the project usage, plan, and billing in the Foursquare console. Heimdall Premium does not cover these charges.
If the provider reports a rate or usage limit, wait for the applicable reset or review your plan. Do not repeatedly retry while limited.
Check the current provider allowance before changing your plan. Heimdall currently makes one Foursquare search request per run.
